8. Mr. syed Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the condemned accused has submitted that though the condemned accused was implicated in the F.I.R. but in the evidence and circumstances detailed below, the learned Additional Sessions Judge ought to have acquitted the accused since the prosecution failed to prove the case against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt. The P. Ws. are all interested whereas no competent and disinterested witness was examined in the case. The occurrence has been alleged to be on the road at Lalanagar infront of the shop of one Bimal Chandra and said Bjmal was not examined which lend support to the defence story that the occurrence took place at the borga paddy land of the informant party belonging to Shayamal which is about 2½ miles off from the alleged place of occurrence. The P. W. 1 is the only eye witness to the occurrence and in his deposition he stated that condemned accused Munshi Meah dealt dagger blow on the neck of the victim About Nabi and the victim died on the spot. P. W. 1 informant Fazal Karim who having stated in the F. I.R. and in his testimony before the court that Munshi Meah also dealt dagger blows in discriminatory on his head and back side of the body at the time of the occurrence when he embraced the condenmed accused Munshi Meah but the same not having been sup by the certificate of the Doctor regarding the injuries on the person of the informant belies the entire prosecution story of inflicting the dagger blow on the person of Abdul Nabi and on the person of the informant P. W. 1 by the condemned accused Munshi Meab. The statements both in the F.I.R. as well as the deposition of the P.W. 1 that the altercation was started between Shayamol Mohajan and the accused party has been belied by the deposition of P. W. 5 who has stated that he has not seen Shayamal at the place of occurrence at the relevant time. The prosecution has failed to prove the alleged motive and incident of altercation and the infliction of dagger blows by Munshi Meah on the neck of Abdul Nabi and also on the person of informant. The place of occurrence being on the road at Lalanagar infront the shop of Bimal @ Monto but the P. Ws. 2, 3, 4 and 5 deposed that they did not see the infliction of the dagger blow on the left neck of Abdul Nabi falsify the entire prosecution story as has been stated by the informant P. W. 1 Fazal Karim as because had there been an occurrence as alleged by P. W. 1 the other P. Ws. who were near the place of occurrence would have witnessed the infliction of dagger blow by Munshi Meah or fleeing of Munshi Meah with or without the dagger. Althoug the dead body of the victim was taken to the Police Stat ion at about 8-30 P. M. on 19.9.87 but the police allegedly seized the wearing apparels of the victim on 20.9.87 at about 8 hrs. from the place of occurrence and in view of the evidence of I.O. that he could not say from whom and from where he has seized those alamats, cast a doubt in the prosecution story of the occurrence at the alleged place of occurrence on 19.9.87 at about 4-30 P. M. The evidence on record revealed that there are houses about 50/60 feets away from the place of occurrence having 200/300 inhabitants but none from the inhabitants was produced before the Trial Court for which adverse presumption ought to have been drawn against the prosecution under provision of 114-G of the Evidence Act. 

 24. Ins in the F. I. R. that upon hearing the hue and cry P. W. Motiur Rahman, Suvash, Arjit, Haron, Nurusufa, Parimal, @ Daniya, Minto and many others came to the place of occurrence and P. W. 1 also admitted that on their hue and cry Matiur Rahman, Suvash, Arjit, Baron, Nurusufa, Parimal alias Daniya, Minto came to the place of occurrence and in is cross-examination of the P.W. 1 that Hathpara is situated-about 50 yards west from the place of occurrence wherein the houses of Reboty, Jogendra, Heron Konja are there. But some of the inehabitants the Nath para of inmate of the houses was examined in the case but P. W. 2 who is the father of the victim, P. Ws. 3, 4, and 5 who have not seen the occurrence inflicting dagger blow on the victim were examined. Non-examination of the disinterested and neutral persons mentioned in the F.I.R. and stated and P. Ws. for the reasons best known to the prosecution and were with-held for which a presumption under section 114 G of the Evidence Act could be drawn against the prosecution and raises a doubt on the prosecution case and the benefit of doubt should be in favour of the accused.
